claims.statement: This AWS guide applies to FPT/GHEC/GHES and describes OIDC federation and the AWS credentials action without storing long-lived AWS secrets; GHES cannot use GitHub-hosted runners.
At this source pin AWS does not support custom OIDC claims; do not assume reusable-workflow custom claims are available to AWS trust.

Provider trust requires a planned security strategy and at least one condition excluding untrusted repositories. Dependabot dynamic event_name is feature-gated to FPT/GHEC/GHES>3.20; GHE.com substitutions are GHEC-only.
For GHES the cloud provider must access discovery and JWKS endpoints; AWS IP-range filtering is an option and the GHES-only note states GitHub does not natively support AWS session tags.
Add the GitHub identity provider to AWS IAM; issuer is the public Actions token URL or GHES hostname service URL. Audience sts.amazonaws.com is specified when using the official AWS action.
The source quotes IAM recommending evaluation of the subject condition for roles trusting GitHub OIDC, then directs adding subject validation to limit which Actions can assume the role.
The branch-specific example uses audience and exact repository/branch subject equality; example organization, repository and branch values are not selected policy.

This AWS guide says repositories created after July15,2026 or opted in use immutable owner/repository IDs in the subject, unavailable on GHES; match the actual subject format rather than copying old name-only examples.
When using an environment the subject must reference its name; environment protection rules are recommended to limit branch/tag deployment and secret access.
The wildcard subject example admits any branch, pull-request merge branch or environment in the named repository; this broader illustration is not approval of that trust scope.
The workflow needs OIDC issuance permission and an AWS action to exchange JWT for cloud credentials; setting the id-token permission to write does not itself grant repository or cloud resource write.

Bucket, region and role are required example substitutions. The sample grants OIDC issuance at workflow root, which is upstream illustration rather than adoption of this project’s draft read-only-root objective.
The example checks out code, invokes a SHA-shaped AWS action reference and copies a file to S3; checkout remains a mutable example tag and no commit origin, cloud role or upload is verified.
The injected comment states the third-party actions are not GitHub-certified and retain separate terms, privacy and support documentation.
Further-reading links are contextual navigation, not additional artifact or runtime credit.

scope: Full pinned article and literal closure read; source propositions are reference-only and do not adopt policy.
